review_notes: I read all 201 lines of Mathlib/Data/DFinsupp/Interval.lean and checked every declaration for vacuity or misstatement: Finset.dfinsupp / card_dfinsupp / mem_dfinsupp_iff / mem_dfinsupp_iff_of_support_subset; DFinsupp.singleton and mem_singleton_apply_iff; DFinsupp.rangeIcc, rangeIcc_apply, mem_rangeIcc_apply_iff, support_rangeIcc_subset; DFinsupp.pi, mem_pi, card_pi; the LocallyFiniteOrder instance and Icc_eq, card_Icc, card_Ico, card_Ioc, card_Ioo, card_uIcc, card_Iic, card_Iio. I compared the statements with the sibling files Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/Interval.lean and Mathlib/Data/Pi/Interval.lean, and checked the building blocks they rely on: LocallyFiniteOrder.ofIcc (Mathlib/Order/Interval/Finset/Defs.lean lines 162-194), DFinsupp support'/support and the lattice/order-bot instances (Mathlib/Data/DFinsupp/Defs.lean line 61-65, 807-808; Mathlib/Data/DFinsupp/Order.lean lines 96-137, 191-206), the elementary interval cardinality lemmas (Mathlib/Order/Interval/Finset/Basic.lean lines 649, 667, 781), and the fact that 0 : Finset α is the scoped singleton {0} (Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Pointwise/Finset/Basic.lean lines 23, 74), which the DFinsupp-of-finsets statements silently depend on. Degenerate cases were checked explicitly and are all handled by the statements: f = g (gives #Icc = 1, so the truncated subtractions in card_Ico/card_Ioc/card_Ioo compute 0 = #Ico = #Ioc = #Ioo); incomparable f and g (the product has a zero factor and the interval is empty, so Nat-subtraction truncation is harmless); empty index type; a value f i = ∅ (then mem_pi is unsatisfiable at i and card_pi's factor is 0). card_Iic/card_Iio have a non-vacuous domain (e.g. α i = ℕ) and their products correctly range only over f.support because 0 = ⊥ forces any g ≤ f to vanish outside f.support. Outside this rubric I noted only minor quality points, not reported as findings: support_rangeIcc_subset is strictly weaker than the equality (rangeIcc f g).support = f.support ∪ g.support available in the Finsupp analogue (Finsupp.rangeIcc_support); the module docstring omits the sibling file's note that these bundled-finset constructions use 0 : Finset α = {0}; and card_Iic's proof mentions the deprecated DFinsupp.bot_eq_zero. I could not run Lean, so all statements above are based on reading and on the stated fact that the file compiles.
